page: Microsoft Azure E96ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, configured with 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs via hyperthreading. Memory capacity is 768.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB per core. The processor includes 480 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware instruction support for AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography extensions (AES, VAES, SHA-NI). No GPU accelerators are provisioned. Local ephemeral storage provides 5,670 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD capacity.

Benchmark results show dominant performance in multi-threaded computation, database handling, and in-memory key-value processing. Multi-core execution scored 101,535.75 on stress-ng and 108,743.76 on the PassMark CPU suite, placing the instance in the top tier of overall throughput. Instruction set extensions and database operations achieved top-decile metrics, with Redis SET operations scaling to 159.97 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth registers at 349.8 GB/sec for uncached read blocks, alongside cached small-block throughput of 7,496.51 GB/sec. LLM prompt ingestion reaches 301.47 tokens per second on 7B models, aided by matrix and vector instruction support.

The qualitative profile demonstrates resource density suited for massive in-memory databases and data pipelines that require rapid local scratch space. The trade-off centers on single-threaded execution, where the 2,292.39 stress-ng score falls into the middle tier, making the architecture less suited for unparallelized single-core bottlenecks. The substantial 768 GB memory footprint combined with 5,670 GB NVMe storage directly accommodates enterprise workloads such as SAP HANA, large-scale relational databases, distributed caching clusters, and high-concurrency ETL pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E96ds_v7 is an enterprise memory-optimized virtual machine driven by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The instance delivers 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores, paired with 768.0 GB of memory to achieve an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. Hardware acceleration covers AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets, backed by a massive 480 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 5,670 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs. Synthetic and real-world benchmarks show top-tier multi-threaded CPU output, 159.97 million Redis operations per second, and strong memory bandwidth capabilities, despite moderate single-core benchmark metrics. The instance is positioned for heavy in-memory databases, large-scale Redis caching, real-time analytics, and high-throughput data processing workflows.
